title: Tell me about yourself
counterpart: Sarah Mitchell, a recruiter at a software company
situation: You are in the first round of an interview for a junior developer role.
opening: Thanks for joining today. To start, could you tell me a bit about yourself?
goal: Give a short, confident introduction linked to the role.

title: Why this company?
counterpart: Daniel Reed, a hiring manager at a logistics firm
situation: You are interviewing for an operations analyst position.
opening: We get a lot of applicants. Why do you want to work here specifically?
goal: Show real knowledge of the company and a clear motivation.

title: Your biggest weakness
counterpart: Priya Nair, an HR business partner
situation: The interviewer wants an honest answer about a weakness.
opening: Everyone has something to improve. What would you say is your biggest weakness?
goal: Be honest and explain what you are doing to improve.

title: A conflict at work
situation: A behavioural interview for a mid-level position.
opening: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a colleague. What happened?
goal: Describe the situation, your action and the result.

title: A failed project
situation: The interviewer is testing how you handle failure.
opening: Can you describe a project that did not go as planned?
goal: Take responsibility and explain what you learned.

title: Salary expectations
counterpart: Mark Evans, a talent acquisition specialist
situation: The final stage of a hiring process.
opening: Before we go further, what are your salary expectations for this role?
goal: Give a sensible range politely and justify it.

title: Why are you leaving?
situation: You currently work at another company.
opening: You have been in your current job for two years. Why do you want to leave?
goal: Stay positive and avoid criticising your employer.

title: Explain a technical idea
situation: You must explain something technical to a non-technical person.
opening: Pretend I know nothing about software. What does an API do?
goal: Explain clearly with a simple example.

title: Working under pressure
situation: The role has tight deadlines.
opening: This team has very busy periods. How do you deal with pressure?
goal: Give a specific example of staying organised.

title: Career plans
situation: The company wants people who will stay.
opening: Where do you see yourself in five years?
goal: Show ambition that fits the company.

title: Questions for the interviewer
situation: The interview is nearly finished.
opening: That's everything from my side. Do you have any questions for me?
goal: Ask two or three thoughtful questions.

title: Urgent report for tomorrow
situation: It is 4:30 pm and your manager needs a report you have not started.
opening: Hi, I need the Q3 sales report by 9 tomorrow. Can you do that?
goal: Agree or negotiate a realistic plan.

title: Extra project on a full week
situation: You already have too much work this week.
opening: Could you also take over the supplier review? Should only be a few days.
goal: Push back politely and propose priorities.

title: Weekend work
situation: A release is at risk and you have family plans on Saturday.
opening: We might need you on Saturday for the release. You're ok with that, right?
goal: Decline or set limits professionally.

title: Status update
situation: Your task is two days behind.
opening: Quick one: where are we with the dashboard? I expected it on Monday.
goal: Explain the delay honestly and give a new date.

title: Asking for feedback
situation: You want to know how you are doing after your first three months.
opening: You wanted to chat? I've got five minutes now.
goal: Ask clearly for specific feedback.

title: Requesting time off
situation: You need a week off during a busy month.
opening: Hey, you mentioned you wanted to ask me something about next month?
goal: Request leave and offer a handover plan.

title: Disagreeing with a decision
situation: Your manager chose a tool you think is wrong.
opening: We're moving everything to the new tracker next week. Any concerns?
goal: Disagree respectfully with reasons.

title: Mistake you made
situation: You sent wrong numbers to a client.
opening: The client says the figures you sent are wrong. What happened?
goal: Own the mistake and propose a fix.

title: Asking for a raise
situation: You have taken on more responsibility this year.
opening: Thanks for booking this. What did you want to talk about?
goal: Make a clear case for a pay rise.

title: Delegated task is unclear
situation: You received vague instructions.
opening: Please clean up the customer data when you get a chance.
goal: Ask clarifying questions about scope and deadline.

title: New priorities
situation: Priorities changed and your current work may be dropped.
opening: Leadership changed direction. Please stop the mobile work for now.
goal: Clarify what happens next and what to do with your work.

title: Colleague misses a deadline
situation: Jake's late part is blocking your work.
opening: Sorry, I haven't finished my part yet. Been crazy busy.
goal: Be firm but friendly and agree a new time.

title: Credit for your work
situation: Rachel presented your idea as her own.
opening: Great meeting, right? People loved the idea!
goal: Raise the issue calmly.

title: Too many messages
situation: Liam interrupts your focus time all day.
opening: Hey, got a sec? Another quick question.
goal: Set a boundary politely.

title: Asking for help
situation: You are stuck on a task and need help.
opening: Hi! You pinged me earlier, what's up?
goal: Explain the problem clearly and ask for help.

title: Covering for a colleague
situation: Omar is going on holiday and wants you to cover his work.
opening: Could you look after my tickets next week while I'm away?
goal: Agree on conditions and get the details.

title: Disagreement on approach
situation: You and Eva want different solutions.
opening: I really think we should remove the filter page. It's confusing.
goal: Discuss and reach a compromise.

title: Onboarding a new hire
situation: Chris just joined and you are their buddy.
opening: Hi, I just started. Where should I begin? Everything's a bit overwhelming.
goal: Welcome them and give clear first steps.

title: Reviewing weak work
situation: Noah's document has many problems.
opening: Did you get a chance to read my draft? Is it good to go?
goal: Give honest, kind, useful feedback.

title: Rude comment in chat
situation: Vanessa was sarcastic about your work in a group chat.
opening: It was just a joke, why are you messaging me about it?
goal: Explain how it landed without escalating.

title: Sharing bad news
situation: Peter's feature will not make the release.
opening: So is my feature definitely in Friday's release?
goal: Deliver the bad news clearly and kindly.

title: Swapping shifts
situation: You need to swap Thursday's on-call shift.
opening: You wanted to talk about the on-call schedule?
goal: Ask for the swap and offer something back.

title: Late delivery
situation: A shipment arrived eight days late.
opening: Our order arrived more than a week late and our production stopped. This is unacceptable.
goal: Apologise, explain and offer a solution.

title: Wrong invoice
situation: An invoice has the wrong amount.
opening: Invoice 4471 is 2,300 euros higher than the agreed price. Please explain.
goal: Investigate and correct it professionally.

title: Service outage
counterpart: David Kim, a client IT manager
situation: Your platform was down for three hours.
opening: Our team lost half a day because of your outage. What are you doing about it?
goal: Take responsibility and describe next steps.

title: Poor quality
situation: A batch of products has defects.
opening: About 15 percent of the last batch is damaged. We expected better.
goal: Acknowledge and agree a replacement.

title: Rude support agent
situation: A customer felt your colleague was rude.
opening: Your support agent was very rude to me on the phone yesterday.
goal: Calm the customer and follow up properly.

title: Missed promise
situation: A feature promised for June is still missing.
opening: We were told this feature would be ready in June. It's now September.
goal: Be honest about the delay and rebuild trust.

title: Threat to cancel
situation: An unhappy client wants to leave.
opening: We are seriously thinking about ending the contract at the end of the month.
goal: Find out why and try to keep the client.

title: Refund demand
situation: A customer wants money back outside the refund period.
opening: I want a full refund. I don't care what your policy says.
goal: Say no kindly or offer an alternative.

title: Data error in a report
situation: A report you delivered contains an error.
opening: The March totals in your report don't match our records at all.
goal: Check the facts and propose a correction.

title: Repeated problem
situation: The same bug came back for the third time.
opening: This is the third time we've reported this problem. Why is it back?
goal: Show accountability and a real fix.

title: Billing confusion
counterpart: Grace Taylor, a small business owner
situation: A customer does not understand the new pricing.
opening: My bill went up and nobody told me. What's going on?
goal: Explain clearly and resolve the concern.

title: Project is behind
situation: Your project is three weeks behind schedule.
opening: I'll be direct: why are we three weeks behind?
goal: Explain causes and present a recovery plan.

title: Scope creep
situation: A stakeholder keeps adding requirements.
opening: Oh, and we also need it to export to PDF. That's easy, right?
goal: Protect the scope and discuss the trade-off.

title: Budget overrun
situation: The project will exceed its budget by 12 percent.
opening: Your forecast shows a 12 percent overrun. How did this happen?
goal: Justify and propose options.

title: Risk nobody sees
situation: You see a serious risk in the plan.
opening: Everything is green on my side. Anything to flag before we report up?
goal: Raise the risk clearly.

title: Dependency on another team
situation: You are blocked by another team.
opening: We're not going to get to your request this sprint, sorry.
goal: Explain the impact and negotiate.

title: Kickoff meeting
counterpart: Laura Bennett, a client project lead
situation: You are opening a new project with a client.
opening: Shall we begin? Maybe you can walk us through how this will work.
goal: Introduce goals, timeline and roles.

title: Unrealistic deadline
situation: Sales promised a date you cannot meet.
opening: I told the customer we'd go live by the 15th. That works, doesn't it?
goal: Reset expectations without blaming.

title: Team member leaves
situation: A key developer resigned during the project.
opening: I heard Marco resigned. What does that mean for your delivery?
goal: Assess the impact and give a plan.

title: Go or no-go
situation: You must recommend whether to launch.
opening: It's your call to recommend. Do we launch on Monday or not?
goal: Give a clear recommendation with reasons.

title: Status to executives
situation: You have two minutes with a senior leader.
opening: I've only got two minutes. Where are we, and what do you need from me?
goal: Give a short, clear executive summary.

title: Lessons learned
situation: A retrospective after a difficult release.
opening: Let's be honest. What went wrong with this release, in your view?
goal: Be constructive and specific.

title: Password reset trouble
situation: A customer cannot log in.
opening: I've tried resetting my password three times and nothing arrives.
goal: Troubleshoot step by step.

title: How do I cancel?
situation: A customer wants to cancel a subscription.
opening: How do I cancel my plan? I can't find it anywhere.
goal: Help them, and ask why they are leaving.

title: Feature request
situation: A customer wants a feature you do not have.
opening: Why can't I export my data to Excel? It seems so basic.
goal: Be honest and offer a workaround.

title: Angry first message
situation: A customer opens the chat already angry.
opening: THIS IS THE WORST APP I HAVE EVER USED. FIX IT NOW.
goal: Stay calm and find the real issue.

title: Shipping question
situation: A parcel seems to be lost.
opening: My tracking hasn't changed in six days. Where is my order?
goal: Reassure and investigate.

title: Upgrade question
situation: A customer is thinking about a paid plan.
opening: What do I actually get if I pay for the Pro plan?
goal: Explain the value without pushing too hard.

title: Bug report
situation: A customer reports a confusing bug.
opening: When I click save, everything disappears. Help!
goal: Collect the details you need.

title: Language barrier
situation: The customer's English is limited.
opening: Sorry my English. Payment no working why?
goal: Use simple, patient language.

title: Duplicate charge
situation: A customer was charged twice.
opening: You charged my card twice this month!
goal: Apologise and explain the refund process.

title: Ask for a discount
situation: A customer asks for a special price.
opening: Your competitor is cheaper. Can you give me 30 percent off?
goal: Respond politely within your limits.

title: Ending the conversation
situation: The problem is solved but the customer keeps chatting.
opening: That worked, thank you! So, anything else I should know?
goal: Close the chat warmly and professionally.

title: Cold call
counterpart: Michael Grant, a busy purchasing manager
situation: You are calling a potential customer for the first time.
opening: Hello, Michael speaking. Who is this? I've got a minute.
goal: Introduce yourself and earn a follow-up.

title: Price is too high
situation: A buyer likes the product but not the price.
opening: It's a good product, but your price is simply too high.
goal: Defend the value and negotiate.

title: Asking for a longer payment term
situation: You want 60-day payment instead of 30.
opening: Our standard terms are 30 days. Why would we change that?
goal: Negotiate better terms.

title: Product demo
situation: You are showing your product to a prospect.
opening: Okay, I've got twenty minutes. Show me why this is better than what we use.
goal: Focus on their needs.

title: Competitor comparison
situation: A prospect is also talking to your competitor.
opening: Your competitor offered us a free first year. Can you match that?
goal: Respond without criticising the competitor.

title: Closing a deal
situation: The deal is close but not signed.
opening: We're nearly there, but I need to think about it a bit more.
goal: Find the final objection and agree next steps.

title: Renewing a contract
situation: A contract renews next month.
opening: Our contract ends next month. Honestly, we're not sure about renewing.
goal: Understand concerns and propose renewal.

title: Upselling
situation: A happy client could benefit from more.
opening: Everything's going well, so why did you want to call me?
goal: Suggest an upgrade naturally.

title: Delivery negotiation
situation: You need a faster delivery at the same price.
opening: Next-day delivery will cost you extra, you know that.
goal: Find a deal that works for both.

title: Partnership proposal
situation: You are proposing a partnership.
opening: Your email was interesting. What exactly do you have in mind?
goal: Explain the benefit to both companies.

title: Following up after silence
situation: A prospect stopped replying.
opening: Oh, hi. Sorry, I never got back to you, did I?
goal: Restart the conversation without pressure.

title: Performance review
situation: Your annual review meeting.
opening: Before I share my view, how do you think this year went?
goal: Reflect honestly and give examples.

title: Receiving criticism
situation: Your manager thinks your updates are unclear.
opening: I've noticed your updates are often hard to follow.
goal: Accept feedback and ask how to improve.

title: Reporting a problem
situation: A colleague regularly makes others uncomfortable.
opening: Thanks for coming. You said you wanted to raise something in confidence?
goal: Describe the issue factually.

title: Giving feedback to your report
counterpart: Daniel Osei, someone on your team
situation: You manage Daniel, who is often late.
opening: You asked to see me? Is something wrong?
goal: Be direct, fair and supportive.

title: Resignation
situation: You have accepted another job.
opening: You look serious. What's on your mind?
goal: Resign professionally and offer a handover.

title: Promotion discussion
situation: You want to move to a senior role.
opening: You asked about the senior position. Why do you think you're ready?
goal: Make your case with evidence.

title: Flexible working request
situation: You want to work from home three days a week.
opening: So you'd like to change your working pattern. Tell me more.
goal: Explain why and how it would work.

title: Exit interview
situation: It is your last week.
opening: We're sorry to see you go. What could we have done better?
goal: Give honest, constructive feedback.

title: Team layoffs
situation: There are rumours and you are the team lead.
opening: People are saying there'll be layoffs. Do you know anything?
goal: Be honest without sharing confidential details.

title: Mentoring session
situation: You are mentoring a graduate.
opening: I feel like I'm not learning fast enough. What should I do?
goal: Encourage and give practical advice.

title: Probation meeting
situation: The end of your six-month probation.
opening: Your probation ends this week. How have you found it?
goal: Summarise your progress and ask about next steps.

title: Internet problems
situation: Your connection dropped during a meeting.
opening: We lost you in the middle of your update. Everything ok?
goal: Explain and catch up on what you missed.

title: Laptop broke
situation: Your laptop died before a presentation.
opening: IT Support here. What seems to be the problem?
goal: Explain the issue and its urgency.

title: Time zone clash
counterpart: Yuki Mori, a colleague in Tokyo
situation: Meetings are always at a bad time for one of you.
opening: Could we move the weekly sync? It's 11 pm for me.
goal: Find a time that works for both.

title: Security warning
situation: You clicked a suspicious link.
opening: Our system flagged a click on a phishing link from your account.
goal: Report exactly what happened.

title: Camera on or off
situation: You usually keep your camera off.
opening: I've noticed your camera's always off in meetings. Any reason?
goal: Explain and agree on an approach.

title: Access request
situation: You need access to a restricted system.
opening: You requested admin access to production. Why do you need it?
goal: Justify the request clearly.

title: Working across cultures
situation: Your direct message was taken badly.
opening: Your last message felt quite aggressive, to be honest.
goal: Clarify your intention and repair things.

title: Software rollout
situation: You are helping a user with a new tool.
opening: I hate this new system. The old one was so much better.
goal: Listen and help them adapt.

title: Forgot a meeting
situation: You missed a meeting you had accepted.
opening: We waited ten minutes for you this morning. Did you forget?
goal: Apologise and reschedule.

title: Sharing a file
situation: A colleague cannot open your document.
opening: That link says I don't have permission. Can you fix it?
goal: Solve it and confirm.

title: Pitching a process change
situation: You think the team has too many meetings.
opening: You said you had an idea about our meetings?
goal: Propose the change with benefits.

title: Interrupted while speaking
situation: Frank keeps interrupting you.
opening: Sorry, just to jump in here, I think what we really need is...
goal: Take back the floor politely.

title: Presenting results
situation: You are presenting quarterly results.
opening: Please go ahead. What are the main takeaways?
goal: Present the key points clearly.

title: A hard question
situation: An executive challenges your numbers.
opening: Where do these numbers come from? They look optimistic.
goal: Answer confidently or admit what you do not know.

title: Running a meeting
situation: You are chairing and the meeting is going off topic.
opening: That reminds me of the office move, has anyone heard about that?
goal: Bring the meeting back on track.

title: Summarising actions
situation: A meeting is ending without clear outcomes.
opening: Okay, I think we're out of time. What did we decide?
goal: Summarise decisions and owners.

title: Asking for clarification
situation: You did not understand a point.
opening: So with the accrual moved to Q4, we should be fine. Everyone clear?
goal: Ask for clarification without embarrassment.

title: Pitching an idea
counterpart: Angela Price, a head of product
situation: You have one chance to pitch your idea.
opening: You wanted five minutes. What's the idea?
goal: Pitch the problem, solution and benefit.

title: Disagreeing in public
situation: A senior manager said something incorrect.
opening: As we all know, customers don't use that feature at all.
goal: Correct it tactfully.

title: Small talk before a call
situation: Waiting for others to join a call.
opening: Hi there! Looks like we're the first ones. How's your week going?
goal: Make natural small talk.

title: Technical problems in a demo
situation: Your demo has stopped working.
opening: It seems to have frozen on my screen. Is that normal?
goal: Handle it calmly and continue.

title: Thanking the team
situation: You are closing a successful project.
opening: So that's it, the project is finished. Do you want to say a few words?
goal: Give a short, sincere thank-you.
